headings: 练习 14 - 书写题与标准答案
diagnostic.tailText: 标准答案用通常的电子枪近似：电子离开阴极时的初速度可忽略，在真空中通过整个加速电压且没有碰撞等能量损失，先作非相对论计算。初速可忽略、无损失和非相对论近似都是解题假设，不是原题另给的数据。令 UUU 为阳极相对阴极的正加速电压，eee 为电子电荷量的大小，取约定的近似常数 e=1.60×10−19 Ce=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}e=1.60×10−19C、me=9.11×10−31 kgm_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}me​=9.11×10−31kg；它们是常用物理常数的舍入值，不是源题印刷的数值。电子向较高电势的阳极加速，获得的动能为 eUeUeU，于是12mev2=eU,v=2eUme.\frac12m_ev^2=eU,\qquad v=\sqrt{\frac{2eU}{m_e}}.21​me​v2=eU,v=me​2eU​​.分别代入题给的两种电压，得到U=500 V:v≈1.33×107 m/s,U=5000 V:v≈4.19×107 m/s.\begin{aligned}U=500\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx1.33\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s},\\U=5000\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx4.19\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}.\end{aligned}U=500V:U=5000V:​v≈1.33×107m/s,v≈4.19×107m/s.​这是上述模型下的两个近似速度，不能当作不论初速和损失如何都必然得到的精确速度。若初速度 v0v_0v0​ 不可忽略，无损失的非相对论公式应为 v=v02+2eU/mev=\sqrt{v_0^2+2eU/m_e}v=v02​+2eU/me​​；题目没有给出可用于另一组数值的初速度。还应区分近似精度：取约定的 c=3.00×108 m/sc=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}c=3.00×108m/s，5000伏特的非相对论结果约为 0.14c0.14c0.14c。若需要相对论修正，在同样初速可忽略、无损失的条件下，应使用v=c1−(1+eUmec2)−2.v=c\sqrt{1-\left(1+\frac{eU}{m_ec^2}\right)^{-2}}.v=c1−(1+me​c2eU​)−2​.用上述舍入常数，5000伏特时相对论速度约为 4.16×107 m/s4.16\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}4.16×107m/s。这说明非相对论值是学校题的近似结果，不是精密相对论值；两种计算都保留了原来的500伏特和5000伏特题设。

headings: Exercise 14 - Written Questions and Standard Answers
diagnostic.tailText: Standard answerUse the usual electron-gun approximation: the electron's initial speed on leaving the cathode is negligible, it traverses the full accelerating voltage in vacuum without energy loss from collisions or other processes, and the first calculation is nonrelativistic. Negligible initial speed, no losses, and the nonrelativistic approximation are modeling assumptions, not extra data printed in the original question. Let UUU be the positive accelerating voltage of the anode relative to the cathode and eee the magnitude of the electron's charge. Use the conventional rounded constants e=1.60×10−19 Ce=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}e=1.60×10−19C and me=9.11×10−31 kgm_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}me​=9.11×10−31kg. These are rounded standard physical constants, not numbers supplied by the source prompt.As the electron accelerates toward the higher-potential anode, it gains kinetic energy eUeUeU, giving12mev2=eU,v=2eUme.\frac12m_ev^2=eU,\qquad v=\sqrt{\frac{2eU}{m_e}}.21​me​v2=eU,v=me​2eU​​.Substituting each of the two stated voltages givesU=500 V:v≈1.33×107 m/s,U=5000 V:v≈4.19×107 m/s.\begin{aligned}U=500\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx1.33\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s},\\U=5000\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx4.19\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}.\end{aligned}U=500V:U=5000V:​v≈1.33×107m/s,v≈4.19×107m/s.​These are the two approximate speeds under the stated model, not exact speeds independent of initial motion or losses. If the initial speed v0v_0v0​ is appreciable, the loss-free nonrelativistic formula is v=v02+2eU/mev=\sqrt{v_0^2+2eU/m_e}v=v02​+2eU/me​​. The question supplies no initial speed with which to calculate a different numerical pair.The approximation's accuracy also matters. With the conventional value c=3.00×108 m/sc=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}c=3.00×108m/s, the nonrelativistic result at 5000 volts is about 0.14c0.14c0.14c. If a relativistic correction is required, the same negligible-initial-speed, loss-free conditions givev=c1−(1+eUmec2)−2.v=c\sqrt{1-\left(1+\frac{eU}{m_ec^2}\right)^{-2}}.v=c1−(1+me​c2eU​)−2​.Using the rounded constants above, the relativistic speed at 5000 volts is about 4.16×107 m/s4.16\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}4.16×107m/s. Thus the nonrelativistic value is the school-model approximation, not a precision relativistic value. Both calculations retain the original 500-volt and 5000-volt cases.

Standard answerUse the usual electron-gun approximation: the electron's initial speed on leaving the cathode is negligible, it traverses the full accelerating voltage in vacuum without energy loss from collisions or other processes, and the first calculation is nonrelativistic. Negligible initial speed, no losses, and the nonrelativistic approximation are modeling assumptions, not extra data printed in the original question. Let UUU be the positive accelerating voltage of the anode relative to the cathode and eee the magnitude of the electron's charge. Use the conventional rounded constants e=1.60×10−19 Ce=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}e=1.60×10−19C and me=9.11×10−31 kgm_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}me​=9.11×10−31kg. These are rounded standard physical constants, not numbers supplied by the source prompt.
As the electron accelerates toward the higher-potential anode, it gains kinetic energy eUeUeU, giving
12mev2=eU,v=2eUme.\frac12m_ev^2=eU,\qquad v=\sqrt{\frac{2eU}{m_e}}.21​me​v2=eU,v=me​2eU​​.
Substituting each of the two stated voltages gives
U=500 V:v≈1.33×107 m/s,U=5000 V:v≈4.19×107 m/s.\begin{aligned}U=500\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx1.33\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s},\\U=5000\,\mathrm{V}:&\quad v\approx4.19\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}.\end{aligned}U=500V:U=5000V:​v≈1.33×107m/s,v≈4.19×107m/s.​
These are the two approximate speeds under the stated model, not exact speeds independent of initial motion or losses. If the initial speed v0v_0v0​ is appreciable, the loss-free nonrelativistic formula is v=v02+2eU/mev=\sqrt{v_0^2+2eU/m_e}v=v02​+2eU/me​​. The question supplies no initial speed with which to calculate a different numerical pair.
The approximation's accuracy also matters. With the conventional value c=3.00×108 m/sc=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}c=3.00×108m/s, the nonrelativistic result at 5000 volts is about 0.14c0.14c0.14c. If a relativistic correction is required, the same negligible-initial-speed, loss-free conditions give
v=c1−(1+eUmec2)−2.v=c\sqrt{1-\left(1+\frac{eU}{m_ec^2}\right)^{-2}}.v=c1−(1+me​c2eU​)−2​.
Using the rounded constants above, the relativistic speed at 5000 volts is about 4.16×107 m/s4.16\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}4.16×107m/s. Thus the nonrelativistic value is the school-model approximation, not a precision relativistic value. Both calculations retain the original 500-volt and 5000-volt cases.

按通常的理想电镀模型计算：电流恒为 $25\,\mathrm{A}$，通电 $2$ 小时；电流效率取100%，即全部电量用于镍的析出。把题给的 $0.2\,\mathrm{m^2}$ 作为总待镀面积，不因想象零件有两面而再乘以2；假定薄镍层均匀，并用题给密度描述其体积。这些效率和均匀性条件是解题模型，不是题面另给的事实。
时间为 $t=2\times3600\,\mathrm{s}=7200\,\mathrm{s}$。严格使用印刷值 $k=3\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{kg/C}$ 和 $\rho=8.9\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$，法拉第电解定律给出
$$Q=It=25\times7200\,\mathrm{C}=1.8\times10^5\,\mathrm{C},\qquad m=kQ=0.054\,\mathrm{kg}.$$
薄层体积为 $m/\rho$，厚度为体积除以总面积 $A$，所以
$$\begin{aligned}h&=\frac{m}{\rho A}\\&=\frac{0.054}{(8.9\times10^3)\times0.2}\,\mathrm{m}\\&\approx3.03\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m}\\&\approx0.0303\,\mathrm{mm}.\end{aligned}$$
因此，理想均匀镍层的厚度约为0.03毫米。这里的计算位数不表示实际镀层具有这样的测量精度。若镀层不均匀，体积除以总面积仅给出薄层模型下的平均厚度，不能确定各处厚度；若电流效率为 $\eta$，同一模型下厚度应乘以 $\eta$。题目未给出这些实际偏差，不能另造实际厚度或暗换镍的电化当量。

Use the usual ideal plating model: the current is constant at $25\,\mathrm{A}$ for $2$ hours, and the current efficiency is 100%, meaning that all transferred charge is used to deposit nickel. Treat the stated $0.2\,\mathrm{m^2}$ as the total area to be coated; do not multiply it by two by imagining two faces of the part. Assume a thin, uniform layer and use the stated density to relate its mass and volume. These efficiency and uniformity conditions are modeling assumptions, not additional facts printed in the prompt.
The time is $t=2\times3600\,\mathrm{s}=7200\,\mathrm{s}$. Keeping the printed values $k=3\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{kg/C}$ and $\rho=8.9\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$, Faraday's law gives
$$Q=It=25\times7200\,\mathrm{C}=1.8\times10^5\,\mathrm{C},\qquad m=kQ=0.054\,\mathrm{kg}.$$
The thin layer has volume $m/\rho$, and its thickness is this volume divided by the total area $A$, so
$$\begin{aligned}h&=\frac{m}{\rho A}\\&=\frac{0.054}{(8.9\times10^3)\times0.2}\,\mathrm{m}\\&\approx3.03\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m}\\&\approx0.0303\,\mathrm{mm}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus the ideal uniform nickel layer is about 0.03 millimeters thick. The calculation's digits do not imply that an actual coating is measured to that precision. For a nonuniform layer, volume divided by total area gives only the average thickness in the thin-layer model, not the thickness at every point. For current efficiency $\eta$, the thickness in the same model is multiplied by $\eta$. The prompt supplies no such deviations from the ideal model, so no different actual thickness should be invented and the nickel equivalent must not be silently replaced.
